utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please be so kind to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT- 00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Ms. Loukas, I think it is scheduled for today that you continue the cross-examination of Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. And just prior to the witness being brought in, if I might just briefly mention a matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'd just like to formally and publicly thank Your Honours and Mr. Krajisnik and the Prosecution and the Defence team for making it possible on a tight court schedule for me to be able to go to my grandmother's funeral. I can indicate that, of course, as Your Honours are aware, my grandmother died while I was in court, and her funeral was to be the very next day in a village in Greece, and, of course, my mother and three of her sisters being in Australia could not make it in time. So I really appreciate the fact that this was made possible, and I do want to formally and publicly thank Your Honours, Mr. Krajisnik, and the Prosecution and, of course, the -- my Defence team for making that possible. It meant a lot to my mother that I was at her mother's funeral when she could not be there all the way from Australia. And also, I'd indicate, Your Honour, I'm also very grateful and should mention to Ms. Verbeek. It was very difficult at the last minute to organise flights, of course, but through a procession of a flight that landed in Athens at 2.30 a.m. in the morning and another flight left that left at 5.30 a.m. in the morning, and then a ferry and then a taxi, I managed to get to the village at ten to 10, and my grandmother's funeral started at 10.00. So I'd like to also formally and publicly thank Ms. Verbeek for making that possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Loukas. I can only say one thing, that the Chamber, and I take it that the same would have been true for Ms. Verbeek, didn't hesitate one moment to assist you in this matter, which, of course, is very emotional for you and very important. So, I'll not say anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could Mr. Davidovic be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, a declaration which said that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing than the truth. I'd like to remind you of that. And Ms. Loukas will continue her cross-examination. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, I just want to take you to a particular aspect of your statement. There's no need for the statement to be before you, but you indicated that at paragraph 10 of your statement, for the benefit of the Court, that Mr. Predrag Jesuric of the SDS in Bijeljina, now, of course, what you mean there is the Serbian Democratic Party; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, you're telling the Court that Mr. Jesuric was a member of the Serbian democratic party; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a member. He was the man who established the party. He was one of its prominent men, and he later claims that he was never a member. I heard that later on in comments. He said he never actually joined the party although he founded it. Whether he had a membership booklet or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, in your statement that you've acknowledged in court is true and correct, you indicated that -- and I just quote for you what you actually have in your statement: "Both prior to and after the 1990 elections, Dr. Novakovic and Predrag Jesuric of the SDS in Bijeljina repeatedly sought me out and requested that I join their party." Now, that's what you've said in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So in your statement you're clearly saying that Mr. Jesuric was a member of the SDS; are you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not what he said. In paragraph 11 he says -- of his statement he says he did not know whether he was a member or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, but I'm taking him through another portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever conclusion, perhaps you quote literally to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If perhaps we could allow the witness to have the statement in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm happy for that to occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to clarify matters? Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's follow the suggestion of the parties and, of course, if there's any need to further clarify, then you may do so. Ms. Loukas, you guide the witness to the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 10, you indicate there that Predrag Jesuric of the SDS -- you see where I'm talking about there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, of course, you indicate in paragraph 11 that you do not know if he was a member of the SDS. But then you also indicate that he was the main ideologue in the Bijeljina SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So the situation is that you don't really have much to contribute on that topic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection. That's argumentative, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm happy to withdraw it and move on to another topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, you'll recall the last time that we were in court, I -- we were dealing with some allegations that I was putting to you that you, in fact, profited by exploiting Bosniak Muslims during the war. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you claimed, and I told you that you should substantiate that, and you mentioned Mr. Mitrovic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, in fact, I think when I was putting those allegations to you, you indicated that -- and this is at page 41 of the transcript for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution, "It is true that whenever I was in a position to do so, I helped anyone who asked me."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that you wanted to save people. That was basically the tenor of the evidence you gave; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that you were not one of those people who exploited Bosniak Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not. I never allowed myself to do anything like that, anything which would bring me into a situation of reaping benefit; quite the contrary. I had a lot of unpleasantness, and it was at my expense very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You were not one of the people who stole or looted from Bosniak Muslims. That's basically what you're saying, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again. You are trying to insult me in a very bad way. You called me a criminal last time; now you're saying I looted. I don't think that that kind of cross-examination is proper. It is highly unpleasant, and I had a lot of unpleasantness when I went back because of the way you put your questions. Your claims are completely unfounded, and they're demeaning to me as a human being.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, you seized all the furnishings and equipment from the dental office of Dr. Edina Alabaci Hujdurovic in Bijeljina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's nonsense; nothing to do with that. How are you able to say that? I hear that for the first time. What you're saying is complete nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, in fact, Mr. Davidovic, after seeing you on television in Bosnia giving your evidence two weeks ago, Dr. Hujdurvic, Dr. Edina Alabaci Hujdurovic, spoke out on local TV about you doing just that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's impossible. That's pure fabrication and nonsense. Absolute fabrication, invention, and nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask before you continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said it's nonsense, would you say it's nonsense that this person said so on television, or is it nonsense that you say, I was involved in that? That's not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was nonsense that I had any part in that, and that the person had said that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that still does not clarify completely. You can say someone could not say such a thing because I was not involved. You can also say it's impossible that someone said that, not because I was not involved but it's impossible anyhow that someone would have said it on television because there was not such a television programme or whatever. My question is: Do you say this person couldn't have said it because "I was not involved", or do you say this was never shown on television that a person said something like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person could never say anything like that nor did she say so, what the lady says, that I took the dental equipment. That's nonsense, and I say with full responsibility that that person would never have said such a thing and never did say such a thing. That's all fabrication, and I'm saying that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, your men actually seized a number of gold bars from the Yellow Wasps during the operation leading to their disbandment. Do you know where that gold is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we captured the Yellow Wasps, there was a quantity of, I think, some two kilogrammes of gold in that part of the operation where the gold was confiscated, and the individuals who confiscated the gold were led by Dragan Andan, the present chief of the police of Republika Srpska, and it was handed over to the SUP in Bijeljina, the gold. And there is a record saying the gold was in the SUP, and there is a commission report on the confiscation of the gold. They weren't gold bars; it was melted-down gold that was found on the individual who was arrested during that operation; in Zvornik, that was. And there is full and complete documentation about the items confiscated, and the commission established that that was kept in the SUP. After I left, several months later, I think that Mr. Macar was head of the commission in the republican MUP, and I have a copy of the minutes, the report and record of that whole event.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you tell the Court that all the gold was handed over, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely correct. I say that with full responsibility. The gold confiscated in the operation in Zvornik was handed over to the SUP. I wasn't in physical contact with it or the people who -- from whom the gold was confiscated. But as I was in charge of the operation, I was informed in detail how the proceedings took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you actually seized the home of Goran Joldic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Property --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean seize a home? How would I do that, seize a house?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Davidovic, that property was placed into the name of your son, Jovica. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know what that's about. Milorad Davidovic, nothing to do with that. I can give you the details of it all, but I have nothing to do with that. During the period of time when that took place, I wasn't in Bijeljina at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Davidovic, there are currently three criminal complaints against you in Bijeljina for serious criminal acts, including business fraud, are there not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm hearing of any such thing from you. That's the first time I've heard anything about it, that criminal proceedings are being taken against me. I've never had anything like that happen to me before, and now you quote three. I never received any papers of that kind at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's leave that aside now, shall we, Mr. Davidovic. You were involved during the war along with your troops in rounding up vehicles in Zvornik and Brcko, which would then be brought to Bijeljina and provided with phoney registration papers. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that when I was in Zvornik and Brcko a number of vehicles were confiscated, but there is documentation on all the vehicles that were confiscated, a receipt of what was taken and where it was stored. When I left Bijeljina, as far as I remember, there were about 300 vehicles in all. I know that in Brcko we drove a large number of vehicles, and we put them on the facilities and compound of where Radio Yugoslavia was located. And I think I said this in my statement, that the heads, the chiefs who were in the MUP of Bijeljina either sold the vehicles or gave them to their friends as gifts. There are reports on all that, documentation on it all. But in addition to those vehicles, there was a full sports hall in the SUP of Bijeljina of items that had been confiscated, the results of looting in Brcko and Zvornik. And when a control was carried out and when the vehicles were stopped, the persons who had confiscated the goods or approach rated the goods had been arrested and the goods were taken. And it was these leaders of this SDS who had come to power who were involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you deny that you profited from this activity, I take it, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, once again, would like to emphasise. Give me the name of any vehicle or tell me of any vehicle, just one single vehicle, that I took to back this up. This is a campaign against me from the moment that I refused to cooperate with the SDS in power, and that is the result of the data gathering to compromise me, and I say with full responsibility that what you're claiming now is a complete lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you are telling lies about Mr. Krajisnik to cover up your own misconduct; that's what I'm putting to you. And I take it you would disagree with me, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I do not wish to comment on those claims made by you. They are your own claims. I am saying what I know about Mr. Krajisnik from my own contacts with him, what I personally saw and what I took part in, and I had contact with Mr. Krajisnik just two or three times, not more. And I told you what I saw. I make no observations to justify myself; I don't see why I should need to justify myself to anybody or to blame anybody to justify myself. So linking up things like that and drawing parallels where I'm concerned on your part is absolutely improper.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't hear your last words. They do not appear on the transcript, Ms. Loukas. I thought that I heard you saying that you had no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. No further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have a small question to you. You have made a lot of assertions, and you have confronted the witness with it. You have not subsequently substantiated by any documents or whatever, the assertions you've made. Is this still something the Chamber could expect to receive? I mean, we are talking about three criminal complaints. One could imagine there is at least some paperwork about that which -- well, would support the assertion you made or -- can we expect something of the kind now or at some later stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that material plus the result of further investigations will, of course, all be dealt with in the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it comes to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the serious nature of those allegations if there is any material now we would like to have that as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, when I said "if it comes to that", of course, if a 98 bis motion will be filed at the end of the prosecution case, of course, the Chamber would like to have available whatever information there is which would either support for challenge the credibility and reliability of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, if there would be any such material, you said it would be presented during the Defence case. The Chamber might be interested to see it already at an earlier stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour. And I can indicate the -- for example, the information about the -- the woman Ms. Edina Alabaci Hujdurovic. That came to light, in fact, over the weekend, and there wasn't enough time to get film here, which, of course, I would have wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But so -- but nevertheless, the information that we have received, we understand to be credible, and whatever further paperwork is provided we will provide that to the Trial Chamber in due course as soon as it becomes available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there also material which stems from a time when the witness had not yet testified because it is imaginable - I'm saying it in these neutral words - that a public testimony triggers whatever support or anti-support --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any material that stems from the times before the witness has testified?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is material. We can gather together that material, Your Honour, and present what we have in documentary form. We can also, Your Honour -- Your Honour understands that this is a matter of continuing investigation, and the information we've received thus far we obviously had an obligation to put to the witness as it was from reliable sources and, Your Honour, of course, the cross- examination couldn't wait any further for further investigations. But as the material -- as the confirmatory material arrives, Your Honour, there is no question that we can place that before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would there be a possibility -- I can imagine Mr. Hannis is also dying to see this material, at least get some impression about it so he can --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Respond appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which could include not responding at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So perhaps the wiser thing to do, if you have not completed that material, first to speak with Mr. Hannis and the Chamber, and then wait and see. It's clear to you that, of course, the Chamber would like to see that material --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the extent that it exists, and we'll see what would then be further needed because if someone says something on television that can be true or cannot be true, and sometimes you need further to find out whether press reports. But we'll hear about press reports soon, whether they would need further exploration, need further investigation, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of course, the Chamber is trying to be as precise as possible in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I go on with some redirect, I would again urge that I have whatever materials are available now. Ms. Loukas had sufficient material to ask those questions. In fairness to this witness and future witnesses who are watching this kind of display, if you're going to come into court and be ambushed and surprised with allegations of such a serious nature, it's important to know whether there is a foundation for that. Future witnesses may call us up and say, I don't want to come because I'm going to be smeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber suggests to the parties that we would have an early break in order to allow Ms. Loukas to further inform Mr. Hannis about the sources which would support her allegations against this witness so that Mr. Hannis also could further inquire to what extent material could be received soon, whether it's written material, when it's expected to come, so as to be better able to choose what his position in this respect will be. Mr. Hannis, is that a suggestion the parties would --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I welcome that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Is Your Honour suggesting we take a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, unless Mr. Hannis would prefer first to put other questions in redirect to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It would be preferable to me to break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I have to look at the clock, because we have started only -- yes. I see both you, Mr. Stewart, and I saw the hand of Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I was only drawing attention to Mr. Krajisnik, Your Honour. That was my only function this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So far, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, is there anything you'd like to add to this procedural suggestion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that before the meeting between Ms. Loukas and the prosecutor, I have a brief meeting with Ms. Loukas for me to provide her with some documents that she can show Mr. Hannis. And afterwards, I should like to be allowed to ask the witness a question, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We did not give you yet an opportunity to do that. We'll have an early break. Ms. Loukas, this gives you the opportunity to consult with Mr. Krajisnik briefly; you're expected to use part of the break, also, to inform Mr. Hannis in more detail after you've spoken to Mr. Krajisnik. And we'll resume at half past three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, before I ask the witness to be brought into the courtroom again, is there anything you'd like to raise as a result of the conversation you had over the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm in a bit of a dilemma. I was handed these documents I have in hand before me. There are seven or eight documents; some have multiple pages. They're all in BCS; I had a language assistant come down. I received these five minutes ago, or six minutes ago, Your Honour; I've had a quick look. From what I was able to gather speaking with the language assistant, it appears to me that some of these don't quite fit in with the way the questions were asked, but I can't tell more without having the opportunity to spend more time with the language assistant. I don't want to hold up proceedings. I have spoken with Mr. Tieger, who indicated he could start with the next witness. I know the Court may be reluctant to stop and start with the next witness, and I really would like to finish with Mr. Davidovic today so he can return home and be done with the proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say -- I don't know how many questions you have. Of course, I would not know how much time Mr. Krajisnik would need, but if we could do that at the last part of today's hearing, then at least you'd have some additional time to prepare and go through the documents with a language assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That would be helpful to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas would there be any --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have a problem with that. I mean, I had a similar problem when I received these documents at the last minute, so I understand it completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Krajisnik, how much time you need to put additional questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a difficult question. I hope that I would be able to finish soon, in 15 or 20 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, of course, the documents are still not entirely clear to you, but would it be a suggestion that we start with giving Mr. Krajisnik an opportunity to put further questions to the witness so that no new surprises would come up? That would then switch to the next witness, and at the end of today's session you could put some questions in redirect. And, of course, if there would be any time needed for further questions from the Bench, we'll see at that moment. Would that be --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That would be agreeable with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Tieger, this is to inform you since you've just entered the courtroom, we will now first give an opportunity to Mr. Krajisnik to put additional questions to the witness. We'll then switch to the next witness. Mr. Hannis will be in a position to have at least one hour, a bit more, to look further at the documents he received and to see whether -- and what questions he would like to put to the witness in redirect. So that would mean for the next witness that he still has to wait for approximately 15 to 30 minutes and that Mr. Davidovic would have to return at the end of today's session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing I'd note is because of the configuration of the courtroom and the limited space, I'll need a few minutes to set things up in between.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. or Madam Usher, would you then escort Mr. Davidovic into the courtroom. Since we are waiting anyhow, perhaps I could already address some few procedural issues. Defence first, I think, the Rule 68 material, which for Witness 280 has been identified by the Defence. The OTP has provided translation, relevant material to be tendered by the Defence as was agreed on the 22nd of June to be tendered at the 27th of June. So the Chamber expects the Defence to tender that material today.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour, in relation to 280. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to 280. I have a few other points, but we'll deal with that at later stage. Mr. Davidovic, as you may have noticed before the break, there was some material to be exchanged between the parties. That has taken place. Meanwhile, the Office of the Prosecution needs a bit more time to look at these documents. We decided that we'll start now by giving Mr. Krajisnik an opportunity to put additional questions to you. He also might confront you with documents; I do not know. Then we'll have a bit of a longer break, and then at the end of today's session we'd like to call you back because then the Office of the Prosecution will have the opportunity to review the materials and might have additional questions, just as the Bench might have. Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, first of all, I extend my greetings to you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I will limit myself to questions that are only related to some documents that will serve to clarify certain issues. If you remember, in your statement you said that from Mr. Djurkovic you saw a document that originated from my office and bore my signature, and that at that point Mr. Djurkovic took the document for himself, and you wanted to have the document. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I have three documents here which clarify certain issues. Since I have only one copy of each, I would kindly ask the usher to place the documents on the ELMO, and if the witness himself can confirm that -- which documents these are. The most important ones are the first and the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to raise -- I'm sorry. I have to raise an objection again to this procedure. We don't receive these documents. They're not in English. They're sprung on us and the witness at the last moment like this. It's -- it's not the best way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the rules apply for you, as well. What have you done in order to seek these documents to be translated so you could provide them to the Prosecution and to the Bench?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These documents were obtained by my Defence team. I only received one copy, and I did not think that I was going to ask questions about them, but I do believe it useful for the witness to take a look at these documents. They relate to one claim that he made in his statement. Perhaps the usher could first place the document before the witness for the witness to see the document first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Krajisnik. Mr. Krajisnik, no. I'd like to see the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, by all means. Your Honour, these are different documents that all relate to one and the same issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, when did you learn about the existence of these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since Mr. Davidovic left. It was in the meantime that this document was obtained by our investigators; The document was provided by Mr. Djurkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the fax I see that it was sent on June the 12th, which was approximately two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Davidovic last testified on June the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I see that it is -- that's the only thing I can see. That must have been a large number of documents. Was it sent to you? Was it sent to Defence counsel? When was it received?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our correspondence goes through the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When did the Defence team receive these documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm informed by my case manager that if it says the 12th, then it would have been the 12th. That's as far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the -- well, of course, it says the fax number, and then a number appears, and then it gives us the date June the 12th. Ms. Loukas, are you in a position to inform us on when Mr. Krajisnik could have known about these documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I will have to get instructions from our case manager about that, and I'll just confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm instructed by my case manager that it would have been received, he assumes, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If it was faxed on the 12th, that would be the Sunday, and I think the 13th was the Monday, and that's when Mr. Davidovic was in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And as, of course, Your Honours are aware, I did indicate then that we were still receiving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but -- so I can establish that these documents, relevant for further questions put to the witness, where he left some two weeks ago are already there for some two weeks, and no attempt whatsoever, at least not to the knowledge of the Chamber, has been made to have these documents translated such as to properly introduce them as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, what I might do -- if I might have the documents in question. I can show them to my case manager and we can have specific information on the specific documents that are being dealt with at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't change the matter that if you want to introduce them as exhibits, that the rule is they should be translated, and especially since most of the documents seem to date from far beyond the indictment period, which, of course, does not make them per se irrelevant, but I can't see that at this moment. Let me just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, may I take it that you consider that it's not necessary to confront the witness with these documents that are available to the Defence, or --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I can just check what the particular documents are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I'll give the documents to you, Ms. Loukas, at this moment so that you can look at what they are. Then, Mr. Krajisnik, you must have been aware meanwhile, and especially in view of this witness who was here to testify two weeks ago, that you can't just -- two weeks later where you had all opportunity even to ask the assistance of the Chamber to have them translated; they are relatively short documents. So, therefore, we'll first give them to Ms. Loukas; then we'll return them to you. You may put questions to the witness, and you may, of course, consult these documents yourself to specify your questions, and if at a later stage it would become perfectly clear that these documents, although mainly from 1993, 1994, 1995, would play such an important role, then we can reconsider if they would be tendered again, then, as documents with the translation attached to it. Madam Usher, would you please give them to Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we're getting now into the realm of an advocate's forensic decisions, but, Your Honour, the dates in question on the documents made them documents that I made a forensic decision not to cross-examine on, being outside the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please return the documents to Mr. Krajisnik. Mr. Krajisnik, you may, of course, refer to events if they are to the knowledge of the witness described in these documents, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]:

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I will try to put questions to you based on this document that you will not be able to see. Do you know the document that you have seen, when it dates from?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Do you know who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you claim that what Mr. Djurkovic had said, that he did not receive the document from me but from somebody else, that it was true?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Djurkovic is such a character that I am simply not able to say anything about him or about what he claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Very well. I forgot to say that we should make a pause between question and answer to allow the interpreters to do their job.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You said that you provided security to the government at Bistrica. Can you tell us if this is something that you stated in your statement? What was the time period that you spent at Bistrica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been May or June. As soon as I arrived at Vrace, I went down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Just talk the time period.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was about the time period, the one that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: This is a document from the OTP, the minutes from the 27th session of the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina held on the 13 June 1992, number 01245366 - it's in Serbian - up until 01245370. And I kindly ask the following: This is a government document, and page 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Let's first see whether we can retrieve the document either in computerised form.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We're getting the little hourglass up on the screen, indicating that the computer is working, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say the computer is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Trying to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any specific portion? Usually these documents, minutes of government meetings, are somewhere in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Many of them are. I was just consulting with Mr. Tieger if he recalled if this one was introduced. He knows a couple of the June 1992 government sessions are in evidence, but we're not sure about this particular day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you mind if a specific portion would be put in evidence and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, then, let's put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, this appears to be in evidence already in Exhibit P65: Mr. Treanor's binder 12, tab number 162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It comes not as a total surprise that it's in the Treanor material. Witness, if you look at the original, then we'll have a look at the translation. Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Page 4 in Serbian, please. I'd kindly ask the witness to read out the portion that was highlighted so that it could be read out in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please draw our attention. It sometimes gives numbers, re: 6, re: 7. Is it a numbered paragraph? Well, let's -- let the witness start read the highlighted portion, and we'll see whether we can find it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The issue of housing the government in Bistrica has been raised." Does this suffice?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If on the 13th of June the government discussed its relocation to Bistrica, would you then claim that you had provided security to some other institution or some other team of people?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not possible that some other organ was involved because it says here the issue of housing the government in Bistrica has been raised. I know for a fact at the time I was there the government was put up there; I spent ten days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown another minutes of the government dated 24 March 1992, 012 of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused read out the number too quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until 01245304.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do have a copy of the document, Mr. Krajisnik? Madam Usher, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- if you haven't got anything else, we have to do with it for the time being, and let's see whether we can find Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It appears that this one was not previously induced, Your Honour. It is in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll first -- is that also a --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is in a footnote to Mr. Treanor's report, but it was not part of the presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would look at a specific portion, have it translated by the interpreters, Mr. Hannis, would you have insurmountable objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I don't object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would now, please, the B/C/S version be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All these are footnotes of Mr. Treanor's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it, Mr. Krajisnik, that you would invite the witness to slowly read the highlighted portion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to read the highlighted part out where it says, "Decision: Rjesenje."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 1: "A decision should be issued to the effect that the ministry of finance should temporarily be housed on the premises of the culture centre of Famos Korin [phoen] ; the ministry of Defence on the premises of the Municipal Assembly; ministry for agriculture, forestry, and water resources management on the premises of the forestry company Jahorina Pale; Ministry of Justice on the institute for the analysis of formaldehyde, and the ministry of health care on the premises of the Korin hospital; the ministry of traffic and communications on the premises of the SOIMEREC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you see now that the government was temporarily housed at Pale and not at Bistrica, that only ten days later the issue was discussed for -- of its relocation to Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the decision was taken that the government should temporarily be relocated to Jahorina. I do not wish to comment on this document because I'm not familiar with the specifics. I was -- I was at Bistrica providing security there for the government for ten days, and there were people there. After all, there was Mico Stanisic there, who issued assignments to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I ask you the following, that you provided security for the government members who slept at Bistrica, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there all day long, from morning to evening and spent the night there. I don't know what they were doing there, but they were there all the time. There were even members of their family there, and there were businessmen who showed up there asking for some papers, and I witnessed it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and I would like to tender these documents into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I have a look at the ... I announced the document as dating the 24th of March, 1992. Madam Usher, could you please put it on the ELMO. Cover page, please. It seems to be a 24th of April, 1992, document which is more consistent with your observations about three weeks later, which I had some difficulties to reconcile late March and 13th of June with three weeks. Would there be any objection to have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I believe it's already in. It's part of Mr. Treanor's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's a footnote, and it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is a footnote to his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then it is in evidence already. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the earlier one had that exhibit number I announced on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's, then, clear. Mr. Krajisnik, there would be no need to have it admitted into evidence again since I do understand it's already under the Treanor material. I, of course, could not check the translation. You two times used the word "relocation," whereas the official translation of the document case "housing," which is not exactly the same. Raising an issue of housing does not necessarily include relocation. Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have misspoke, but I believe that I did say 24 April. There must have been an error in interpretation, but I'm glad that we've clarified the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You said that the leadership of Republika Srpska supported the paramilitary formation. I would now like to go back to the document presented to you by the OTP which is P777, 00845558, which is a report to the president of the republic, Mr. Karadzic, by Mr. Adnan. Could the witness read the last page and comment on it. If necessary, or maybe it would be a good solution to place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have an English translation, and perhaps the English translation should be put on the ELMO, and the original B/C/S document should be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Witness, could you read out the footnote written by Mr. Karadzic in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Radovan Karadzic," although I saw the handwriting the first day a few days ago with the Prosecution, it says here, "Carry on or keep enforcing order and the rule of law, law and order," and I can't read what it says in brackets. "Keep enforcing law and order." That piece of information came from us. We wrote it; we compiled it and sent it on to the government. And as far as I know there was a discussion held at the Assembly with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you know that there was no debate in the Assembly because last time Ms. Loukas showed you a document from the 10th session, Assembly session, but the material, the document went to the government and someone from Mr. Karadzic came, and this was a note by the person who showed him the document, the material in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. If he's talking about the session I think he is, I believe it was the 20th session, but could we have some clarification about which session and what date he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I considered that issue to have been completed last time. The witness said that at a session in September or October, which was the only session, that Kerovic discussed something about the introduction of law and order, and that he discussed Mr. Davidovic. And then Ms. Loukas brought the stenographic notes from the session, and we were able to see that Mr. Davidovic wasn't mentioned at all. If we need bring in the minutes from that session, we will do so because that's the only one that the Prosecution did not have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's true. We did not have the full minutes of that session. I believe Defence counsel had the B/C/S version last time. We haven't received it and translated it yet to see what's in there. But as you recall, Your Honour, when we had this discussion it was not -- Mr. Davidovic did not say that it occurred at the session. He said that Mr. Meakicic told him it was discussed at the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's as such clear. Mr. Krajisnik, you may put a question to the witness. You're not allowed to tell the witness what he knows as you did on approximately one page ago when you said, "Witness, you know that there was," and then -- please put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Trial Chamber allow me to send the minutes of that session and to have it translated subsequently if it hasn't been translated because Ms. Loukas's question related to that matter last time, and there was no discussion. All -- everything had been cleared up. Now I hear that it hasn't been cleared up and it is -- we're still discussing whether Meakicic said anything or not and whether Mr. Karganovic said something or not. Now, we can take a break and bring in the minutes from that Assembly session to allow the witness have a look and clear the matter up again once on for all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you may put a question to the witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, I'm sure you'll remember that you said that equipment arrived by helicopter, MUP helicopters to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I should like to ask the next document, that is to say a conversation between Cedo Kljajic and Pero Mihajlovic to be placed in front of the witness; 03220299, used by the Prosecution in the trial. May that document be provided? 03220229, and the page is 03220231. It is a conversation between the two men about the equipment. So may we have that document provided in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, it appears that was Exhibit 766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Or .A.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read part of the text for the witness, and I'm going to ask the witness to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: On the second page of the B/C/S, page 2, towards the end, Pero Mihajlovic says the following -- have you found that, Witness? "Momo didn't order that for the Serb MUP but for the other one," and then on the next page Cedo Kljajic says, "Yes, yes, yes." Pero Mihajlovic says, "So that should all be stopped." And Cedo Kljajic says, "Certainly, sure." Pero Mihajlovic says, "All of it. Because they called me, I will stop it all now." Cedo Kljajic says, "Well, if you could bring that to us here, we could make further arrangements, you know." Now, my question is this: Do you know about that procurement of Mr. Mandic's for the BH of MUP, MUP BH?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that it was about procuring some passports and documents that are issued in the department in Belgrade, and Pero was in charge of contacts at the mint because that's where the passports were issued and other documents issued by the Ministry of the Interior. It is special documents printed on special forms, et cetera. So that's what Pero is referring to, those documents that Mandic had ordered previously, whether he should go ahead with that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Witness, the conversation took place on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Did Bosnia-Herzegovina need Yugoslav passports at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They issued Yugoslav passports for the whole of that year and later on in 1992 afterwards, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Do you understand it, then, that it was not equipment brought in by helicopter but what all this was about was passports?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that equipment had been ordered from Momo Mandic through the federal SUP because the federal institute for the issuance of money asked for other documents and passports; the institute for legal tender, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could you keep your answers brief, please. Now, you're not linking this conversation up to the equipment that arrived at Pale by helicopter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. I'm not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that I and my escorts had collected money for the citizens and from the customs. For what was this, and what date was that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was informed about that when I arrived at the border crossing. I think it was the Christmas holidays or just before the Christmas holidays and New Year holidays, and they told me that you were there with your escort, that you had taken some money, and you said that that was for government purposes or state purposes, and that you signed a receipt and then left. And that's what I said, that I received that information from the customs officer at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you give us the name of that customs officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember his name. I tried to remember it. I did my best, but I just can't remember the name because they would come and do their shift and leave. They would change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I've understood you correctly, it's the border crossing where?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Bosansko Raca. Yes. And it was money that was paid by citizens working abroad. They were taxed 200 marks per month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Don't give us a speech. Just tell us where the border crossing was and what year.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I see, 1993. Thank you. Now, I put it to you -- if I put it to you that I never took the money, then do you still remain by your claims, assertions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the information I heard. I can't say whether you took the money or didn't take the money. I can't believe you or not believe you. It's open for interpretation. I can only say what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Right. Thank you, but I'd like to ask you to keep your answers short, please, in view of the limited time we have. I have another document here, now, which was sent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, if there's any need that you think that a witness should not deliver speeches but answer your questions, you may address me so that I can judge on whether there's any need to say such a thing to the witness, and I'll do it if I think it's justified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the Trial Chamber, and thank you for your advice and guidelines on that point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: A document was used here, a review of events and the situation assessment of the situation in Brcko; 00741394 was the document's number. The signature is the War Presidency of Brcko municipality. And you commented on the document. Does the Prosecution have the English version of that document? Or let me ask the question: Do you remember the document, Witness, and, if so, have you ever seen the document? Did you ever see it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about at all. I can't remember, so I can't really say. I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, do you have a B/C/S copy of that document so that it could be presented to the witness, or would you have --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, this was Exhibit number 22, which came in through our first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm looking to see if I have a copy here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Was that document ever in your possession?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: So you didn't receive the document from anybody; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember talking about the Assembly when the Vance-Owen Plan was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you remember what you said, how you were dressed on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Throughout the whole time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I were to show you a CD now, a tape -- or rather, can we have this CD played? It is footage showing Mr. Davidovic in civilian clothing on the tape at the Assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is brand new. I don't know what the provenance of this. I don't know what date it is. I don't know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know how long he's had it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope it is necessary to ascertain the truth, to see whether the witness is right in what he says or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the question was a different one. What's the provenance of that tape?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our investigators found the whole stenographic notes of the Assembly, and they also found video footage of the beginning of the meeting where you can see Mr. Davidovic, and I brought that first part. But, of course, we can hand in the entire tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anyway to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 95, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is 95. Is there anyway to identify the date by viewing this video?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will be able to see the individuals, Mr. Mitsotakis, Mr. Milosevic, Mr. Bulatovic; you see it all on the tape. It's Jahorina, and it will say on the tape what Assembly session it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I recall Mr. Davidovic's statement, he talked about attending a deputies' club meeting which was, as I understand it, the day before the Assembly session. And as I understood it that's what he was talking about, not the Assembly session but the deputies' club meeting the night before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness today whether he was -- or rather, what he was wearing. He said he was in camouflage uniform all the time at Pale, but it's -- a lot of years have passed by since then, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked the witness, "Can you remember what you said, how were you addressed on the occasion." The answer was, "I was wearing camouflage uniform." And then the question was, "Throughout the whole time?" "Yes, the whole time." That could easily be understood as to be the whole time at the occasion, since you limited your question to that. Since when do you have that CD in your possession, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This compact disk was brought in by hand; they couldn't send it. But in the meantime I had other witnesses, so I prepared myself when I found the time. Had I known, I would have really sent it in on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since when do you have it was the question, Mr. Krajisnik, not on how you received it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since after Mr. Davidovic's departure. That's when I received the compact disk. I don't remember the exact time, but a visitor visiting The Hague was supposed to bring it in. Maybe it was sent in on another date; I can't actually say for sure now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive it through Defence counsel, or did you receive it directly from a visitor?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from Mr. Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karganovic, could you inform the Chamber on when you gave this CD to Mr. Krajisnik, or could you please answer that through Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please inform Ms. Loukas, who deals with this witness, on when you gave the CD Mr. Krajisnik is referring to, to him. If you would please inform Ms. Loukas so she can address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Karganovic doesn't have a specific recollection, but what he can do is check his e-mails, and then he can discover precisely when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that, then, during the break perhaps, and most -- if Mr. -- first of all, we can't play a CD just unannounced. That seems to cause technical problems. If Mr. Krajisnik would be willing to give the CD temporarily to Mr. Hannis so that he could have a look at it and put it on the pile together with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise a point? If we could ask Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the witness to take his headphones off for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Davidovic, would you please take your headphones off.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I gather the point that's trying to be made is Mr. Davidovic said he was wearing camouflage during the event, which I thought him to understand being the deputies' club meeting at midnight the day before the Assembly session, and Mr. Krajisnik wants to play a video showing him the next day at the Assembly session wearing civilian clothes. That's not very helpful to the Tribunal unless you ask him, did you also wear camouflage clothing during the Assembly session meeting the next day? Because, indeed, he could have changed clothes from the night before to the morning after, which was a more formal occasion with the visiting dignitaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Hannis suggests you to put a question to the witness. Do you follow that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, on the day of the session itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness now has his earphones on again. Mr. Krajisnik, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, on the day of the session itself, were you in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes because I had other assignments at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we don't need to have the CD played. That solves that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you to tell me this: What did the session decide, what matters?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About whether the Vance-Owen Plan was to be accepted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Just brief answers. So it was about the Vance-Owen Plan. Tell us the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Did we vote for or against the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't know that, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You were there, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- came and went. I wasn't there the whole time to follow the whole of the Assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I think this is a matter of record. It's not very helpful to have this witness comment on what's in the minutes of that Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I think that there are reliable ways of establishing what happened during that session. Do you have any further questions, Mr. Krajisnik? You indicated that you hoped you would do within a quarter of an hour. I have some difficulties to understand how you could have formed that opinion, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I'll be able to get through it quickly. I apologise, Your Honour, but I just have to ask a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you gave -- made many comments about the session itself, so it's not that you didn't know what was going on. So please answer me this: Tell me -- or, rather, what was the voting like? How did the deputies vote?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Very well. Now, do you know why we rejected the Vance-Owen Plan or whether we rejected it at all?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the Vance-Owen Plan was not accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know about Milosevic and Cosic's interactions and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I say to you, I put it to you that we confirmed a previous decision and put it to referendum, if I were to tell you that would you have a different opinion or, rather, would you be opposed to that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I tell you that there was individual voting and that we stated our views and confirmed a Bijeljina decision taken previously by which the decision needed to go to a referendum, that is to say that the citizens should state their views about the Vance-Owen Plan at a referendum, would you accept that? Do you have different knowledge, or do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. All I know was that the plan wasn't accepted, and that's how it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Davidovic, that at the time we confirmed our decision, the Bijeljina decision, and handed over the whole issue and matter to a referendum. Now, did your people tell you that, the people you talked to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that when the Assembly session was over we prevented the journalists from entering the Assembly hall and that President Cosic asked Milosevic, Slobodan, he said, what should I tell the journalists now? I don't know how to react. And he said -- Mr. Cosic said, We'll see what's been done, what's going to be done in the future, and then he left and went back to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: If I told you that the Vance-Owen Plan was to abolish Republika Srpska, would you change your opinion in condemning the deputies for handing over the whole thing to a referendum?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not well-placed and don't have the capabilities of commenting on matters like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Now, my last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This material, Your Honour, is a document with signatures. It was sent to the International Red Cross. It is a Muslim petition asking to be relocated. I would like to ask the Trial Chamber's advice. Can a document of this kind be tendered into evidence or used in this court at all? May I have the Court's guidance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Documents as such are not excluded from being admitted into evidence, but if you want to do it through this witness, then at least this witness should know something about this document; otherwise, we could consider whether there are other ways of introducing it into evidence. But if you want to do it through this witness, the witness should have any knowledge about the document. What makes you believe, Mr. Krajisnik, that this witness would have any knowledge of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness spoke about the fact that the Muslims left the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Ethnic cleansing. Now, this document speaks about the way in which the Muslims left Bijeljina, and it is signed and stamped by the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's first put it to the witness. Let's just confront him with the document and ask whether he has any knowledge about the document. But perhaps I'd first have a look myself. Mr. Krajisnik, could you tell us where this document is stamped by the International Red Cross? I see that halfway the document there's an empty page, and then there's a card, which is from someone associated with the International Red Cross. But the document itself, I do not see any stamp because that's how you introduced it. Could you please tell me where I find such a stamp, apart from one page just in the middle where a card of a person associated with the Red Cross is found?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The title itself, Your Honour, is a petition sent to the International Red Cross, and this contributes to Mr. Djurkovic's statement, who was in charge of population exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. You may ask the witness. I see that it's addressed, but you said it's stamped, which is something totally different. Would you please put the -- one of the other problems is that the first page appears, I think, seven or eight times and then only we move to -- could you please, Madam Usher, show the cover page and then this, one of the following pages, to the witness, and I'll first ask the witness whether he has any knowledge of it. No, if you -- Witness, my question to you is have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't, but I have heard about this document. I heard about it, and I can explain to you its origins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Krajisnik would like to ask you the origin of this document you've never seen before, then it seems to be a relatively short text, and then we have long pages of names. And, Mr. Krajisnik, if you would like to ask the witness, and you said this was your last question, you may do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I forgot. I have another question, which is the last one and a very brief one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you are aware of the fact that Mr. Djurkovic effected the exchanges of the Muslim population through the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when the looting and murders became public and some people were compromised, and when the Muslims were taken to the border between Serbia and Hungary, that was when the international community got involved because it saw that everything went out of control and sought to prevent such negative conduct. I can explain to you in detail how these things went along, if you wish. You know, and regardless of the fact that this is a very heavy statement to make but this is true, you know that the SDS conducted, planned a systematic relocation of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Please, could you specifically answer my question related to that document.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Muslim houses started being broken into, their property seized, and so on, the international community started exerting pressure through the International Red Cross.
